title: Four women suspected of desecrating children's graves for "paranormal session"
excerpt: Four women stood trial in the Utrecht district court on Wednesday on suspicion of desecrating the graves of children at the Rusthof cemetery in Leusden, which falls under Amersfoort. content:
Thursday, 29 October 2026 - 12:50

Four women stood trial in the Utrecht district court on Wednesday on suspicion of desecrating the graves of children at the Rusthof cemetery in Leusden, which falls under Amersfoort. They held a “paranormal session” on the children’s graves in 2021. 58 people pressed charges against them, RTL Nieuws reported.

In 2021, the group attempted to communicate with the spirits of the deceased children by placing small, colored, orb-like lights on their graves and asking them questions, like “Did you like soccer? Could you make the light go on?” The manager of the Rusthof cemetery had granted permission for the séance.

The matter came to light when someone found a video camera containing footage of the séance at the cemetery. This caused a great deal of unrest. Several families had their loved ones reburied at a different resting place, at the municipality of Amersfoort’s expense. An investigation by the National Ombudsman concluded that the cemetery management took insufficient account of what impact such an activity would have on surviving loved ones when allowing the séance. The municipality ultimately removed the director of the cemetery from his position.

A mother of one of the deceased children read a victim statement in court on Wednesday. “We live not only with the loss, but also with the question about exactly what took place. What was said, and what was touched? Why was this done in a place where children are laid to rest?” She explained that her trust in the cemetery had been shattered. “We left our child there because we believed it was a safe place,” she said.

She asked for symbolic compensation of €1. “The true damage we have suffered is incalculable and irreparable,” she said. “It affects us, our family, and our friends every single day.”

The Public Prosecution Service (OM) recommended up to 200 hours of community service against the four women. Only one attended the trial: 81-year-old Irene B. from Hoevelaken. She heard the lowest sentence recommendation: 40 hours of community service, half of which is conditionally suspended.

“It is a deeply unsettling feeling that such action took place at the cemetery where your loved one lies,” the public prosecutor said in court, according to RTV Utrecht. He spoke of an extraordinary case, noting that the court must determine whether a paranormal session constitutes a form of grave desecration.

The court will rule soon.
